text:
Owen Power is playing 26:14 a night, more than four and a half minutes above last season, and Buffalo looks better for it. He has 14 points in 16 games after 0.36 points a game last season, capped by three assists against Columbus. The Sabres take 54.8 percent of the expected goals with him on the ice at 5v5, 9 points better than without him.

This is the version of Power people imagined when Buffalo took him first overall in 2021. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 96th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists last season, so the playmaking was there; it was waiting for the minutes. Evolving-Hockey had him at replacement level in actual wins but 1.3 in expected wins, another sign the chances were better than the results.

Twelve of his 14 points are assists, his goals match his chances, and none of it relies on his power-play time. The thing to watch is the defensive side of all those minutes against top lines. So far, so good.
headline: Owen Power finally has the job the first pick should have
